newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli army denies shelling Lebanese port.
newsitem.headline: Israeli army denies shelling Lebanese port.

text.p: Israel's army said on Monday it was not behind the shelling of Lebanon's southern port city of Sidon in which six civilians were killed and 34 were wounded.
"The Israeli army did not fire towards Sidon," an army statement said. It said forces under the command of pro-Israeli militia leader Antoine Lahd were behind the attack.

Lahd is commander of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) in an Israeli-held occupation zone and of a militia force in the Jezzine area just outside the zone. The army said this second group was responsible.
"General Lahd's forces in the Jezzine area carried out the firing," the statement said.

"The SLA is backed by Israel whereas the people who fired are not backed by Israel," an Israeli military source insisted. Military sources said the shelling followed an increase in attacks on the Jezzine area.
The Israeli army said two Lebanese youths were killed and two wounded hours earlier when an explosive device blew up a vehicle in the Jezzine area.
The army said Hizbollah, the Iranian-backed "Party of God", carried out the attack.
Security sources in Lebanon said some of the 34 wounded civilians were seriously hurt in the three rounds of shelling on Sidon.
Israel and its SLA allies patrol a 15 km (nine mile) deep border zone set up inside Lebanon with the declared aim of preventing guerrilla attacks on Israel's northern border.
